title: Command-Line Arguments
subtopics: Passing arguments when launching a program
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of command-line arguments and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—using string[] args—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study command-line arguments with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you turn raw console input into validated data and provide clear feedback for invalid values. In this lesson, focus on using string[] args and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: String values are immutable sequences of text. Use value equality for text content, understand Unicode code points for international text, and prefer StringBuilder for repeated concatenation in loops. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect using string[] args with passing arguments when launching a program before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently.

items.title: Building small command-line utilities
items.text: Treat console input as untrusted text. Validate format and range before using it, account for token-versus-line reading, and give users a clear way to correct invalid input.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
